title: Rust code with Java-style trait/factory layering
task: Review a Rust module that introduces a trait, boxed dynamic dispatch, factory, adapter, and service wrapper around one concrete local implementation.
context: No plugin or runtime substitution boundary exists.
The trait mirrors the concrete type methods one-for-one.
The factory always returns Box<dyn Repository>.
The concrete type could be constructed directly without changing behavior.
evidence: Repository search finds no second implementation.
No caller depends on dynamic dispatch.
Tests exercise behavior without requiring substitution.
The abstraction adds heap allocation and indirection.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep the architecture because dependency inversion is always cleaner.
Add more traits so every concrete type has an interface.
Prefer dynamic dispatch simply because it looks more abstract.
expected_decision_properties: Recommend simplifying toward direct concrete construction for the current context.
Recognize that Rust traits are useful when they define a real capability or substitution boundary, not as mandatory interfaces.
Avoid unnecessary Box<dyn Trait> when static concrete code is sufficient.
Preserve the option to introduce a trait later if a real provider or polymorphic boundary appears.
unacceptable_reasoning: Rust should copy Java-style interface layering.
Every dependency should be represented by a trait.
Dynamic dispatch is automatically more maintainable.
verification_expectations: Run clippy/type checking used by the repository.
Confirm no caller requires runtime substitution.
revisit_when: A second real repository implementation appears.
A plugin/provider boundary requires runtime substitution.
Independent test substitution becomes a real architectural requirement.
